cards.b: Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions as work progresses.
A source you create from direct experience, such as your own drawing or photograph.
An image or information made by someone else, such as a book or website.
Drawing what you see directly in front of you.
The size relationships between parts of an object.
Hold pencil at arm's length, arm locked; measure one part and compare others to it.
Drawing the gaps around and between objects to check shapes and proportions.
Drawing the outline without looking at the paper; builds observation and expressive line.
A quick 30 second to 2 minute drawing capturing movement and pose.
All depth lines meet at one vanishing point on the horizon.
A frame (card or phone camera) used to choose and crop a composition.
A focus question that guides what you record, for example how light changes an object.
Photo collages of one scene from many viewpoints; shows several moments and angles.
Repeated, scratchy lines drawn again and again to search for the form.
AO3 should continue as work progresses; new studies show development and relevance.

short.q: Explain why AO3 needs your own observation.
short.model: Own observation shows genuine skill and personal insight, and is first-hand evidence that examiners can credit; copying other people's images shows little.

short.q: Describe how to start an accurate observational drawing.
short.model: Use light construction lines and basic shapes, measure proportions with a pencil at arm's length, check with plumb lines and negative space, then add detail.

short.q: Give two ways to show variety in recording.
short.model: Use different media (pencil, charcoal, pen), different viewpoints and crops, photographs, notes, rubbings or blind contour studies.

short.q: How can you make recording relevant to your intentions?
short.model: State a line of enquiry and choose subjects, viewpoints and techniques that explore it, adding short notes linking each study to your aim.
points: choices and notes linked to aim

short.q: Describe how Hockney's photographic joiners could inspire your recording.
short.model: Take many overlapping photos of one subject from different positions and assemble them to show several viewpoints, then draw from the result.
